chunks: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Ibn Sahl (Harun ibn Muhammad) Zanjalah narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us from Sa'd ibn Sa'id from Abi Tayyibah from Nur ibn Wabarah from al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) from Jibril from Israfil from His Lord, May He be glorified and exalted, that He said:

Whoever prays on the night of Eid al-Fitr ten rak'at, reciting in each rak'ah the Opening of the Book and 'Say: He is Allah, One' ten times, and says in his bowing and prostration: 'Glory be to Allah, and all praise is for Allah, and there is no god but Allah, and Allah is the Greatest.' Then he recites the Tashahhud and gives Salam between every two rak'at.
When he finishes from them, he says a thousand times: 'I seek forgiveness of Allah and I repent to Him.'

Then he prostrates and says in his prostration: 'O Ever-Living, O Sustainer, O Possessor of Majesty and Honor, O Merciful of the world and Compassionate of the Hereafter, O Most Generous of the generous, O Most Merciful of the merciful, O God of the first and the last, forgive my sins and accept my fasting, my prayer, and my standing (in prayer).'

And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'By the One who sent me as a Prophet with the truth, he does not raise his head from prostration until Allah forgives him and accepts from him the month of Ramadan and overlooks his sins, even if he had committed seventy sins, each of which is greater than the sins of all the servants.'

I said: 'O Jibril, does He accept from him specifically the month of Ramadan, or from all His servants in his lands?' He said: 'Yes, and by the One who sent you with the truth as a Prophet, O Muhammad, indeed among His honor upon Allah and the greatness of his status is that He accepts from him and from them, and accepts from all the monotheists between the East and the West their prayers and their fasting, and forgives their sins and answers their supplications.'

After informing him of this, and by the One who sent me with the truth, indeed whoever prays this prayer and seeks forgiveness with this seeking of forgiveness, Allah will accept his prayer, his fasting, and his standing, and forgive him and answer his supplication.

Because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said in His Book: 'And ask forgiveness of your Lord; then turn to Him in repentance.' And He said: 'And those who, when they commit an immorality or wrong themselves, remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins.' And who forgives sins except Allah? And He said: 'Seek forgiveness of Allah; indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.' And He said: 'Seek forgiveness of Him; indeed He is the Accepting of Repentance.'
And the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'This is a gift for me and my Ummah specifically from men and women, and He did not give it to any of the prophets who were before me, nor to others.'
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for praying ten rak'at on the night of Eid al-Fitr according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A'mal* outlines a specific night prayer (Salat al-Layl) for Eid al-Fitr, emphasizing the chain of transmission from Allah through the archangels to the Prophet, which underscores its divine origin. It highlights the immense spiritual reward of complete forgiveness and acceptance of Ramadan worship, contingent upon sincere repentance (Tawbah) and prolonged prostration (Sujud), a practice deeply valued in Shia devotional life for seeking divine mercy. The text uniquely claims this ritual as a special gift exclusive to the Prophet's Ummah, distinguishing it from previous prophets.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. It was narrated to us by Muhammad b. Ibrahim who said it was narrated to us by Ibn Sahl Harun b. Muhammad Zanjalah who said it was narrated to us by Abu al-Abbas Ahmad b. Hameed who said it was narrated to us by Abu Salih from Sa’d b. Sa’eed from Abi Tayyibah from Nur b. Wabarah from al-Rabee’ b. Khatheem from Abdillah b. Mas’ud from The Prophet (s.a.w.s.) from Jibra’il from Israfeel from His Lord May He be glorified and exalted that he said:
‘and ask His forgiveness; surely He is oft-returning (to mercy).’
This gift is special to me and my Ummah. The prophets and their people before me did not get this gift.”
